lndian Standard
SODIUM SPECIFICATION FOR CARBONATE, MONOHYDRATE, PHOTOGRAPHIC GRADE

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
Standards Materials Division

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian on SO-June 1987, after the draft finalized by the Photographic Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Council.

0.2 This Indian Standard is one of a series of specifications for photographic grade chemicals which are commonly used in the processing of sensitized photographic materials. These specifications have been preparetl to establish criteria of purity which will provide a practical and economical grade and prevent possible faulty processing which might be caused by chemicals of inferior quality and to furnish the manufacturers, suppliers and processors with reliable and readily available specifications for photographic chemicals of satisfactory quality. 0.3 Sodium carbonate, sensitized photographic developers, particularly ents is very essential formula NazCOa.H~O monohydrate is used in the processing of materials. It finds use in preparing photographic in colour films where high purity of rhe ingrediand extremely important. It has a chemical and molecular mass 124.

0.4 This Indian Standard was first published by the Acids, Alkali and Halides Sectional Committee in 1971 and had covered the material for use in pharmaceutical and antibiotic industry along with that for photographic industry. the material suitable for only In the present revision, photographic industry has been covered and accordingly, the title of the standard has also been modified. In the present standard, the requirement for assay has been modified and the requirements for free alkali, bicarbonate and reaction to ammonical silver nitrate have been added. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated,. expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 3

IS : 6155 - 1987 accordance with IS : 2-1960'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for sodium carbonate, monohydrate, photographic grade used in processing of sensitized photographic materials. 2. REQUIREMENTS 2.1 Description - Sodium carbonate, monohydrate, photographic grade shall'be in the form of white crystalline free flowing granules, free from lumps and external visible impurities. 2.2 Solution in Water - 29 g of the material dissolved in 100 ml of distilled water at room temperature shall give a clear and colourless solution free from sediments other than a slight flocculence. 2.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements given Table 1 when tested according to the methods given in Appendix A.

. 3. PACKING AND MARKING in air-tight cdhtafnrrs the purchaser and the closed and marked

3.1 Packing - The material shall be packed with a plastic liner or as agreed to between supplier. 3.2 Marking - Each container shall legibly and indelibly with the following a) Name c) Name e) Date 3.2.1 of the material; in the package; and trade-mark, number; of manufacture. may also be marked b) Mass~of the material d) Lot or batch The containers

be securely information:

NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau The of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to co rlply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and aupervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard -Mark mav be granted to manufacturers or porcessors may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

4. SAMPLING 4.1 The method of drawing respresentative test samples of the material and the criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in Appendix B.

B-3. TEST SAMPLES

AND REFEREE
Samples

SAMPLE

B-3.1 Preparation

of Test

B-3.1.1 Draw with -an appropriate sampling instrument, a small portion of the material from different parts of each container selected. from each container shall be The total quantity of the material drawn sufficient to conduct the tests for the characteristics given in Table I and should be about 400 g.

B-3.1.2 Thoroughly mix all portions of the material drawn from the same container. Out of these portions, a small but equal quantity shall be taken from each selected container and shall be well mixed up together so as to form a composite sample weighing not less than 800 g. This composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the supplier and the third to be used as referee sample. B-3.1.3 The remaining portion of the material from each container ( after a small quantity needed for the formation of composite sample has been taken ) shall be divided into three equal parts, each part weighing not less than 50 g. These parts shall be immediately transferred to thoroughly dried bottles which are then sealed air-tight with stoppers and labelled with all the particulars of sampling gi-ven under B-1.6. The material in each such sealed bottle shall constitute an These individual samples shall be separated individual test sample. into three identical sets of samples in such a way that each set has an individual test sample representing each container selected. One of these another to the supplier and the three sets shallbe sent to the purchaser, third shall be used as a referee sample. B-3.2 Referee Sample - The referee sample shall consist of the composite sample ( see B-3.1.2 ) and a set of individual samples ( see B-3.1.3 ) marked for this purpose and shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the supplier. These shall be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier and shall be used in case of dispute between the two. B-4. NUMBER OF TESTS by mass,
